title: Presidential system of government
competency: Define the presidential system and compare it with the parliamentary system.

keywords.def: A system where a directly elected president is head of state and government, separate from and not accountable to the legislature.
The legislature's power to vote to remove a president who violated the oath of office.

en.text: In a presidential system the people elect the president and the legislature separately. The president is head of both state and government, serves a fixed term and is not accountable to the legislature. Features: superior position of the president, separation of powers with checks and balances, impeachment, and a fixed term (in the USA, four years, at most two terms).

screens.ask: Block 14 households voted for their council AND their chairperson. Both answer to the households. Is the chairperson accountable to the council?
opts: No, both answer to the households
